newsitem.title: INDIA: Possible petrol price hike pulls down India shares.
newsitem.headline: Possible petrol price hike pulls down India shares.

text.p: ** Indian stocks close broadly lower, as
worries about possible hike in petroleum product
prices weigh down market
** Bombay's shr index falls 44.93 pts, 1.18 pct to 3,756.78
** ICICI announces 62 pct rise in 1996/97 net profits,
aluminimum major-Hindalco profits fall 2.5 pct
** State-run Bank of India 6.67 billion shr issue traded at
60.70 rupees each compared to 45 rupees issue price
** National exchange index down 23.50 pts at 1,045.5,Delhi
17.70 pts to 772.84 and Calcutta 1.57 pts to 105.21
Blue chips at Bombay exchanges ended near the day's lowest levels on Monday, as fears of a possible hike in prices of petroleum products pulled down prices, dealers said.
"The market was pretty bearish. There was no good news to push up prices," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage.

Term-lending institution Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) posted a 62 percent jump in 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 7.7 billion rupees, after adjustment for previous year balances. ICIC shares rose three percent to end at 59.50 rupees, and up from the day's low of 56.50.
The results are post-merger figures. ICICI announced a merger with SCICI in January, but the merger took effect from April 1, 1996.
Market action was lacklustre, with buyers staying on the sidelines, participants said.
"The impending (petroleum) price hike made people little bearish in the short-term," said Govind Agarwal, institutional sales dealer at Motilal Oswal Securities.
"The market broke a technical barrier of 3,798. The next support level should be around the 3,700 level."

Shares of Bank of India were heavily traded on the first day of listing at the Bombay exchange. More than 2.13 million shares changed hands, with the stock ending at 60.60 rupees against an issue price of 45 rupees, traders said.
The state-run bank which raised 6.75 billion rupees in February through an inital public offering of equity was traded at 50.25 rupees minutes after opening at the Bombay exchange.
Shares of Hindalco ended three percent lower at 907.0 rupees. The firm announced a 2.5 percent fall in 1996/97 net profit to 3.91 billion rupees after the close of trading hours.
State-run BHEL rose 18.50 rupees, or 4.6 percent to 419.75.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
